verdict.rationale: Databricks documents an official CLI for interacting with the platform from a terminal or automation scripts, with versioned migration guidance and subcommands like `databricks air run` for submitting GPU workloads. A hands-on runtime probe confirms the AI-native angle: `databricks aitools install` wrote 29 vendor agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others. Missing for 10: evidence of machine-friendly behavior such as structured/JSON output and non-interactive auth, plus independent community corroboration of CLI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: The Databricks CLI (command-line interface) allows you to interact with the Databricks platform from your local terminal or automation scripts.
Define a workload's compute, environment, and command in YAML, then submit it with databricks air run.
the Databricks CLI SHIPS vendor agent skills — `databricks aitools install --path /tmp/pa-dbx-skills` keylessly wrote 29 plain SKILL.md skill folders
To migrate from Databricks CLI version 0.18 or below to Databricks CLI version 0.205 or above, see Databricks CLI migration.
